extracted.intended_audience: aspiring public relations counsel, PR practitioners, corporate and association executives
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical criteria for practicing as a public relations counsel: understanding public opinion, choosing and using communication instruments, advising clients on policy and action, and conducting ethical, constructive publicity campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study the public mind
rubrics_metrics.description: “The public relations counsel is first of all a student. His field of study is the public mind.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the facts of life as textbooks: newspaper and magazine articles, advertisements, billboards, speeches, sermons, gossip, theater patter and other public expressions as primary sources for understanding public attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitiveness to state of public mind
rubrics_metrics.description: “Now sensitiveness to the state of mind of the public is a difficult thing to achieve or maintain.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a specialized ability—akin to a clinical sense—through painstaking self-criticism and experience to estimate group reactions over wide geographic and psychological areas; combine intuition with systematic tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ research campaigns, symposiums and surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: “He employs the research campaign, the symposium, the survey of a particular group or of a particular state of mind as a further aid, and confirmation or modification of his own appraisals and judgments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative and qualitative research to confirm or modify intuitive judgments; treat surveys and symposiums as tools for evidence-based PR decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use diversified communication instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: “There are the instruments by which he broadcasts facts and ideas to the public; advertising, motion pictures, circular letters, booklets, handbills, speeches, meetings, parades, news articles, magazine articles and whatever other mediums there are through which public attention is reached and influenced.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and combine media (press, radio, lectures, stage, motion pictures, mail, advertising, events) appropriate to audience and objective; do not rely on a single medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper training and knowledge of public tastes
rubrics_metrics.description: “The competent public relations counsel has generally had some newspaper training...the value of this training ‘is a keen sense of the likes and dislikes of what we call the public’.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop familiarity with press norms and public tastes to craft copy and pitches that editors and audiences will accept; newsroom experience is especially valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise on actions and policy, not only messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: “He is becoming to-day as much of an adviser on actions as he is the communicator of these actions to the public.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend changes to client policies and practices (not just communications) when public point of view changes; align organizational action with public expectations to avoid reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent clients from drifting into harmful situations
rubrics_metrics.description: “...to keep them from drifting inadvertently into unfortunate or harmful situations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act proactively as risk manager: monitor developments and advise early interventions to avert crises or backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create circumstances and events
rubrics_metrics.description: “First of all, there are the circumstances and events he helps to create.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and stage events or circumstances that shape news and public perception (press events, parades, exhibits, publicity stunts) as part of strategic campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret the public to the client and the client to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: “He acts in this capacity as a consultant both in interpreting the public to his client and in helping to interpret his client to the public.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve a bidirectional role: translate public sentiments into actionable advice for clients and translate client objectives into messages the public will understand and accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor informal channels and hourly events
rubrics_metrics.description: “He must be alive to the events of the day — not only the events that are printed but the events which are forming hour by hour, as reported in the words that are spoken on the street, in the smoking cars, in the school room...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously listen to informal, grassroots discourse (conversations, local networks) as well as formal media to detect nascent issues and shifting sentiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professional standards distinct from ‘publicity man’
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish ‘counsel on public relations’ from the old ‘publicity man’ whose practice was to get ‘something for nothing from publishers’; a true counsel ‘has one of the most important jobs on the roster of any concern.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt ethical, constructive, and strategic practice rather than transactional or manipulative publicity tactics; seek credibility and long-term trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a constructive force in the community
rubrics_metrics.description: “The public relations consultant is ideally a constructive force in the community. The results of his work are often accelerated interest in matters of value and importance to the social, economic or political life of the community.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame campaigns to produce social value and public benefit where possible; emphasize constructive outcomes, not merely client advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publicity for public education and corrective campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Health department example: publicity is a major function because constructive work depends on public education in combating evils and building cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design PR campaigns that inform and educate (e.g., health, safety) and that correct misunderstandings or harmful impressions about industries or institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise clients to consider social and operational factors
rubrics_metrics.description: “He must either himself appraise the public mind...He may to-day consider, for instance, in his sales campaign, not only the quality of his soap but the working conditions, the hours of labor, even the living conditions of the men who make it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and advise on underlying operational or social issues (labor practices, production conditions) that influence public perception; PR must integrate with corporate responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate with civic, industry, and community movements
rubrics_metrics.description: PR departments coöperate with Welcome Stranger Committee, conventions, children's camps, and similar movements to build goodwill and practical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forge partnerships with civic organizations, conventions, and community initiatives to create positive public-facing programs and goodwill gestures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate public relations within associations and industry programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade associations include among functions: general publicity, industrial bureau, legislative work, exhibits, research — and forty associations have incorporated public relations with general publicity as definite parts of their program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed PR functions (publicity, research, exhibits, foreign trade bureaus) within associative structures to coordinate industry-wide public messaging and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publicity to shape international and political opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Lithuania example: issued pamphlets, paraded, figured in pictures and motion pictures to develop favorable sentiment and ultimately achieve freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage international propaganda/publicity tools (pamphlets, parades, pictures, motion pictures) strategically to influence foreign and political audiences when stakes require it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt to increased public scrutiny and democratic information demands
rubrics_metrics.description: “The public to-day demands information and expects also to be accepted as judge and jury... The willingness to spend thousands of dollars in obtaining professional advice on how best to present one’s views or products to a public is based on this fact.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that publics are more literate and expect transparency; craft strategies that meet higher expectations for information and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain close contact with the press as primary medium
rubrics_metrics.description: “So long as the press remains the greatest single medium for reaching the public mind, the work of the public relations counsel will necessarily have close contacts with the work of the journalist.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate journalist relationships, understand news cycles and editorial needs, and use press channels effectively while combining them with other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on both intuition and empirical confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The counsel brings the talent of his intuitive understanding to the aid of his practical and psychological tests and surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance intuitive, experience-based judgments with empirical tests (surveys, research campaigns) to avoid self-deception and to validate strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary function: advise how positive results can be accomplished
rubrics_metrics.description: “His primary function now is not to bring his clients by chance to the public’s attention...but to advise his clients how positive results can be accomplished in the field of public relations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on strategic planning and measurable outcomes rather than serendipitous publicity; set objectives and design campaigns to achieve them.
